fd5a090e4b55: Prezentacja krok po kroku: alfabet, dwie litery i jeden dźwięk, ogonki, dwa zapisy jednego dźwięku, akcent, typowe błędy.
18e30e07b6ff: Dziś przeczytasz na głos każde polskie słowo. Today you'll read any Polish word aloud.
6c015253f078: Ciekawostka. The Polish alphabet has 32 letters, and there is no q, v, x — they only appear in foreign words. Instead, there are nine letters with «tails» and strokes: ą ć ę ł ń ó ś ź ż.
5bb9043966a2: Start with the green letters — they read the same as in English. Then the blue, pink and purple ones. After each group there's a mini-check «Sprawdź się».
ed22ee969d8e: Ciekawostka. ó and u sound the same today — like «oo» in English «book». Long ago ó was a long «o», which is why Poles still write stół, though they say «stoow». In the same way, rz and ż, ch and h sound the same.
bf454910ada0: A word plays — choose the letter it contains. 12 questions; points and your streak of correct answers are counted.
7c8f2ab14c11: Ciekawostka. In trzy, after t the letter pair rz loses its voice and sounds like «sh»: «tshy». And ę in pięć and dziesięć is read as «en» before ć: «pyench».
d8aac3af8f6c: Tap each number, then play them all in a row and count aloud along with the recording.
eb9619738ada: Two short conversations: at a Polish course and in a shop. Tap a line, repeat it aloud, then act out the conversation with your teacher — first with your first name, then spelling your surname letter by letter.
ccdcd7819cdd: 14 words and phrases from the lesson. They go into your word deck on the site.
cbb1705bc509: Four real little texts: a price list, an SMS, a shopping list and a greeting. First read aloud, then tap the card and check yourself.
d4b8752db30c: Ciekawostka. As late as the first half of the 20th century, ł was pronounced like a regular «l» in many regions. Now it sounds like English w: Łódź sounds like «Wooch», and Wrocław like «Vrotswaf».
30c73530a9da: Board the Intercity train: tap a city — the train will travel through the stations on the way. Every word on the city card can be tapped. Look for mountains, lakes, rivers and Poland's neighbours on the map.
e0967d342874: 18 words — from kawa to three names Poles use to scare foreigners: Szczecin · Wrocław · Szczebrzeszyn. Read each one aloud and tap «Umiem». The clock keeps time, and your record is saved.
cd750366d720: Ciekawostka. Szczebrzeszyn is a real little town in the Lublin region. Every Pole knows it thanks to Jan Brzechwa's poem about a beetle (chrząszcz), and the town even has a monument to the beetle.
d057b623cf71: 5–7 minutes a day. Three blocks — you only tap, no typing.
eaf4fc72e52f: Open the «Alfabet» trainer every day: tap 🔊 on each letter of a group and repeat the word aloud right away. Then do «Wyzwanie» again and try to beat your record.
